react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological theme: the arachidonic acid eicosanoid cascade. RaMP multi-database ORA identifies Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top hit with an FDR of 6.97×10⁻¹⁴, overlapping all five lipid input metabolites (arachidonic acid, 15-deoxy-Δ¹²'¹⁴-PGJ2, 5-HETE, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE) against a 27-member pathway, giving a fold-enrichment of 1429.7. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (community-standard) places hsa00590 Arachidonic acid metabolism at rank 1 (p=1.0 raw; 4 metabolites hit: arachidonic acid, LTA4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE), confirming the same axis in KEGG namespace. Mummichog m/z-direct activity on the human_mfn network yields Arachidonic acid metabolism as the clear top winner (p=4.20×10⁻⁴) with the highest overlap (11/11 input metabolites resolved), followed by Leukotriene metabolism (p=0.0266) and Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (p=0.0343) — all downstream branches of the same cascade. The cross-paradigm consensus is unambiguous: five of the seven inputs are canonical eicosanoids, all stemming from arachidonic acid via 5-lipoxygenase (5-HETE, LTA4), 15-lipoxygenase (15-HETE), and COX-mediated branches (15d-PGJ2). Phenytoin (a voltage-gated sodium-channel blocker) and 3-methyladenine (an autophagy inhibitor) did not map to any eicosanoid pathway in any paradigm and may represent off-target metabolic liabilities or indirect regulatory effects. Arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219) is the upstream substrate and primary driver; its oxidative products 5-HETE (KEGG:C04805) and 15-HETE (KEGG:C04742) are the most informative downstream reporters of pathway activation.
